item_description: A hot Jupiter orbiting the Sun-like star 51 Pegasi, notable as the first exoplanet discovered around a Sun-like star.
item_facts: It was announced in 1995 by Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz.
The planet orbits very close to its star and completes an orbit in about four days.
It is also known as Dimidium.
needs_review: Verify discovery priority, orbital period and approved proper name against astronomy sources.

item_description: The third planet from the Sun and the only world currently known to support life.
item_facts: Earth has one natural satellite, the Moon.
About 71 percent of Earth’s surface is covered by water.
Earth’s atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen by volume.
needs_review: Verify percentages and current scientific wording with NASA or authoritative Earth science sources.

item_description: A reported super-Earth exoplanet candidate orbiting the red dwarf star Gliese 667 C.
item_facts: Gliese 667 Cc was reported in 2011 using radial-velocity observations.
It is part of a triple-star system in Scorpius.
Its status and orbital parameters have been debated as data analyses changed.
needs_review: High-priority review: confirmation and habitability claims have been debated; check current exoplanet catalogs.

item_description: A hot Jupiter orbiting the star HD 209458 and one of the first exoplanets observed transiting its star.
item_facts: It is also called Osiris.
Its transit was detected in 1999.
Observations of its atmosphere helped establish exoplanet atmospheric spectroscopy.
needs_review: Verify discovery timeline and observational milestones with primary astronomy papers.

item_description: The largest planet in the Solar System, a gas giant with a system of moons and faint rings.
item_facts: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun.
Its Great Red Spot is a long-lived storm, though its size has changed over time.
Jupiter has many confirmed moons; the number changes as new objects are confirmed.
needs_review: Verify current moon count and storm details with NASA or IAU sources.

item_description: A sub-Neptune exoplanet orbiting in the habitable zone of the red dwarf star K2-18.
item_facts: K2-18 b was discovered using the Kepler space telescope’s K2 mission.
The planet’s atmosphere contains detected molecules, though interpretation is ongoing.
Being in a habitable zone does not establish that a planet is habitable or hosts life.
needs_review: Atmospheric claims are evolving and debated; check the latest peer-reviewed studies and avoid life claims.

item_description: A transiting exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of a Sun-like star, discovered by the Kepler mission.
item_facts: NASA announced its discovery in 2011.
It is larger than Earth, but its composition is not known with certainty.
A habitable-zone orbit does not establish surface liquid water or life.
needs_review: Verify discovery details and avoid describing the planet as confirmed Earth-like.

item_description: A confirmed exoplanet orbiting a Sun-like star at a distance that places it in the star’s habitable zone.
item_facts: NASA announced Kepler-452b in 2015.
Its radius is estimated to be larger than Earth’s.
Its mass and composition are not precisely known, so it is not confirmed to be rocky.
needs_review: Verify current planet status and measurements; avoid calling it an Earth twin.

item_description: The fourth planet from the Sun, a rocky world with a thin atmosphere and evidence of ancient water activity.
item_facts: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.
Its surface includes Olympus Mons, the largest known volcano in the Solar System.
Current robotic missions study its geology and climate.
needs_review: Verify comparative superlative and current mission status through NASA/ESA sources.

item_description: The smallest planet and the closest planet to the Sun in the Solar System.
item_facts: Mercury has no substantial atmosphere, only a very thin exosphere.
It has a large iron-rich core.
Despite being closest to the Sun, it is not the hottest planet; Venus is hotter on average.
needs_review: Verify physical details with NASA planetary science sources.

item_description: The eighth planet from the Sun, an ice giant with a deep blue appearance and powerful atmospheric winds.
item_facts: Neptune was discovered in 1846 after mathematical predictions of its position.
It has a large moon named Triton, which orbits in the opposite direction to Neptune’s rotation.
Neptune’s blue color is influenced by atmospheric methane and other factors.
needs_review: Verify discovery history and atmospheric explanations with NASA sources.

item_description: A confirmed exoplanet orbiting Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to the Sun.
item_facts: Proxima Centauri b was announced in 2016.
It orbits within the star’s nominal habitable zone.
Its atmosphere and surface conditions are unknown, and stellar activity may affect habitability.
needs_review: Verify current status and clarify that habitability is unconfirmed.

item_description: The sixth planet from the Sun, a gas giant best known for its bright ring system.
item_facts: Saturn’s rings are made mostly of water-ice particles with a range of sizes.
Saturn has many confirmed moons, including Titan and Enceladus.
The Cassini spacecraft studied Saturn and its system from 2004 to 2017.
needs_review: Verify current moon count and mission dates through NASA sources.

item_description: A roughly Earth-sized exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of the red dwarf star TOI-700.
item_facts: NASA announced TOI-700 d in 2020 using TESS observations.
It is part of a multi-planet system.
Its atmosphere and surface conditions have not been established.
needs_review: Verify parameters and current system discoveries using NASA and peer-reviewed sources.

item_description: One of seven known Earth-sized planets orbiting the ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1.
item_facts: The TRAPPIST-1 system is about 40 light-years away.
TRAPPIST-1e is among the planets receiving an amount of stellar energy that may allow temperate conditions.
An atmosphere or life has not been confirmed there.
needs_review: Verify distance and habitability-zone interpretation; avoid claims of life or known oceans.

item_description: An Earth-sized planet in the TRAPPIST-1 system, orbiting farther from its star than TRAPPIST-1e.
item_facts: TRAPPIST-1f is one of seven planets in the system.
It was detected through transits of its star.
Its atmosphere and surface conditions remain uncertain.
needs_review: Verify orbital and atmospheric information with current research.

item_description: The outermost of the seven known planets in the TRAPPIST-1 system.
item_facts: TRAPPIST-1g was detected using transit observations.
The planet is larger than Earth by radius, though its composition is not known precisely.
Its climate and potential habitability depend on uncertain atmospheric conditions.
needs_review: Verify current planetary parameters and avoid interpreting size as a known composition.

item_description: The seventh planet from the Sun, an ice giant with an unusually tilted rotational axis.
item_facts: Uranus rotates with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees.
It has faint rings and many known moons.
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus up close, during a 1986 flyby.
needs_review: Verify current moon count and orbital/rotation figures with NASA sources.

item_description: The second planet from the Sun, with a dense carbon-dioxide atmosphere and extreme surface temperatures.
item_facts: Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System on average.
Its surface pressure is about 92 times Earth’s sea-level pressure.
Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most planets.
needs_review: Verify atmospheric values and rotation description with NASA planetary sources.

item_description: An extremely hot gas giant orbiting very close to its star, WASP-12.
item_facts: WASP-12b completes an orbit in roughly one Earth day.
The planet is heated intensely by its close orbit.
Observations suggest the planet is distorted by tidal forces from its star.
needs_review: Verify current orbital parameters and tidal interpretation using NASA Exoplanet Archive and papers.
